evidence.quote: Note: By Ordinance, East Brunswick Township does not require or issue a Certificate of Occupancy for residential resale or rentals.

The Township has elected not to implement the permissive portion of the State Code which would require re-inspection before resale or refinancing of single, townhouse or condominium residential dwelling units.
If you have any questions, please call 732-390-6875.
Steven R. Curtis Construction Official scurtis@eastbrunswick.org

resale_co.notes: The Township says in writing that it does not require or issue a certificate of occupancy for residential resales or rentals. Commercial properties are different: a Resale Certificate / New Tenant Certificate is needed for any change of commercial tenant or ownership ($75 processing fee, then $200 and inspections by all 4 subcodes). The smoke/CO certificate from the fire district is still required on every sale.

requirements: Districts 1 and 3: working hardwired or 10 year sealed battery smoke detector on each floor including the basement near the stairs, and within 10 feet of each bedroom; hardwired detectors must stay hardwired; detectors over 10 years old must be replaced; UL listed

Districts 1 and 3: a low voltage fire alarm system needs a passing inspection report from the alarm company, a NJ-certified fire protection contractor or a licensed electrician, shown to the inspector

Districts 1 and 3: CO detector in the hallway within 10 feet of any bedroom if the home has a fuel burning appliance or attached garage; stand-alone CO detectors no more than 7 years old, combination smoke/CO no more than 10 years old
Districts 1 and 3: house numbers at least 4 inches high (or at least 2 inches on both sides of a curbside mailbox), visible from the street and contrasting

District 2: alarm type depends on year built (before 1977 10 year sealed battery; 1977 to 1984 electric; 1984 to 1990 electric interconnected; after 1990 electric interconnected with battery back-up and one in each bedroom); CO alarm within 10 feet of each sleeping area
District 2: secondary power sources (solar, generator, etc.) must be properly labeled (new February 2025)
All districts: portable fire extinguisher recommended, not required (since February 2025)

fire_cert.notes: East Brunswick has three fire districts (DCA registry code D). District #1 runs the Bureau of Fire Safety for Districts #1 and #3 (registry note: FD#1 is the enforcing agency for FD#3). District #2 has its own Bureau of Fire Prevention at 216 Joseph Street. The state fire directory (surveys January to February 2026) lists Jaysen A Whalen and the District #1 office for all three district pages, including District #2; the District #2 website shows its own bureau, forms and fees, so the district's own site is used for District #2. The District #2 site does not name its Fire Marshal. Which district an address is in must be checked; the District #2 site links a Fire District Map (https://maphub.net/EBFD1/east-brunswick-fire-dist-1), which was not opened. The state directory prints the District #1 email as fireofficial@ebfmo.com; the District #1/#3 site (ebfmo.com now redirects to ebfmo.org) lists JWhalen@ebfmo.org, which is used. District #2 also posts a notice that all residences in District #2 need an inspection before any change of occupancy (rentals included). Re-checked 2026-10-06: the District #2 site was redesigned; its district page now labels 732-257-2846 'District Office' (was 'Main Office') and adds an after-hours inspector line (732-354-6484). The Fire Prevention Bureau phone (732-210-4582), email and the September 2026 smoke application fees are unchanged.
